extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in comedy and media controversies; comedians, comedy writers, and media professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and practical guidance about producing and managing shock/taboo comedy—covering timing ('too soon'), audience/context, medium (Twitter/YouTube/live), craft vs persona, and career/PR consequences. Draws on Gilbert Gottfried's experience and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing ('Too soon')
rubrics_metrics.description: The temporal proximity of a joke to a tragic event matters; critics often invoke 'Too soon!' to mark unacceptable timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gottfried: 'Too soon' meant that if I had waited like three more days, the tsunami was forgotten about. Example: his World Trade Center joke immediately before 'The Aristocrats' drew boos and the refrain 'Too soon!'. Timing can determine whether shock lands as release or as offensive misstep; consider how quickly news cycles move and when a topic becomes culturally permissible to joke about.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shock/taboo as a deliberate comedic technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Using taboo subjects and deliberately grating material as a central element of one's act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Everything about Gottfried’s comedy is intended to grate, from his shrieking delivery ... to his material’ — shock is a tool. Carlin: it’s 'the duty of a comedian to find where the line is and cross it.' When done well, crossing the line can produce the biggest laughs; however, it carries heightened risk of outrage and professional consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience and context sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate jokes according to the audience (fans, general public, specific groups) and situational context (roast, funeral, Twitter feed, TV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media framing changes perception: 'They didn’t say “his jokes,” they said, “his comments and remarks.”' Roasts and certain venues tolerate more; mainstream media and casual social platforms may react differently. Know who you are performing for and how context reframes material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform/medium matters for reception and craft
rubrics_metrics.description: The medium (Twitter, YouTube, live stage, television) affects both how material is developed and how it's received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gottfried: 'the line has been erased' on Twitter; online posts spread fast. YouTube can create visibility but may not develop live-comedy skills: 'they haven’t learned to develop anything or how to experience working in front of an audience.' Choose material and tone suitable for the platform and expect different consequences online vs onstage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crafted joke writing versus persona-driven comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between comedians who write and craft jokes and those who primarily perform a quirky persona.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gottfried criticizes the 'new kind of celebrity comic' who 'isn’t crafting jokes, but just trying to create a sort of amusing persona.' Crafted material indicates developed skill and longevity; persona-driven fame (reality TV/viral personalities) can yield visibility and money but may lack depth and stage craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live-performance experience ('developing chops')
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing as a comedian requires performing in front of real audiences to refine timing, delivery, and material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gottfried: if he had YouTube as a teen 'I think I would have terribly undeveloped, unfunny bits.' Anti-pattern: relying solely on recorded/viral clips instead of stage work. Emphasize repeated live practice to learn audience dynamics and edit material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis management: deletion and cover-up perceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Deleting offensive online posts is ineffective and may look like a cover-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gottfried: 'With the Internet, if you erase something it just means you have to spend another half-minute to find it.' Deleting can intensify scrutiny; be prepared with a response strategy rather than relying on erasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent and the comedian’s role in crossing lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the comedian's intent (character, satire, duty to test limits) justifies crossing socially sensitive lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gottfried: 'It’s the duty of a comedian to find where the line is and cross it.' Comedians often appeal to artistic intent; audiences and employers may or may not accept that justification. Reflect on purpose and whether crossing the line advances a comedic point or merely provokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catharsis and social release
rubrics_metrics.description: Taboo jokes can function as a release that helps audiences cope after tragedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Gottfried’s performance of 'The Aristocrats' after 9/11 is described as 'the moment it was OK to laugh again.' Use of taboo for catharsis can be powerful, but timing and framing are crucial to avoid perceptions of callousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional risk versus potential reward
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider career consequences (loss of endorsements, reduced bookings) when using provocative material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gottfried lost his Aflac role and saw potential hiring fallout: 'maybe no one was out-and-out saying, “We’re not hiring you”' but opportunities diminished. Conversely, viral controversy can raise visibility and followers. Weigh long-term reputation and income streams against short-term notoriety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading audience reaction (nervous laughter as signal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use audience cues—like 'that laugh where people laugh extra hard because they don't want to laugh'—to judge whether material has crossed a line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nervous or guilty laughter can indicate taboo transgression that elicits release rather than straightforward amusement; performers should read these signals to decide whether to push further or retreat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material selection and venue-appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose which bits to perform based on the venue, audience expectations, and personal brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gottfried: 'I tell jokes from my dirty jokes DVD, but the “Aristocrats” one I don't tell that much.' Some signature pieces are reserved for appropriate contexts; tailor set lists to fit occasion and audience tolerance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipating media framing and sensationalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect media to reframe comedic remarks in ways that amplify outrage (choice of words, selections of quotes).
